summary: 'Bad address' or 'connecting to host returned an error' can mean the host key isn't in paramiko's known_hosts, since background persistent connections can't prompt; pre-populate with ssh-keyscan or set host_key_auto_add, with care.
questions: Why does my network connection fail with Bad address?
How do I auto-accept SSH host keys for paramiko?

answer_card.title: Fix 'Bad address' host key errors
answer_card.answer_md:
Persistent paramiko connections run in the background and can't answer the host-key prompt. Either pre-populate known_hosts (verify the keys):
```shell
ssh-keyscan veos01
```
or auto-accept (security risk):
```shell
export ANSIBLE_PARAMIKO_HOST_KEY_AUTO_ADD=True
```
```ini
[paramiko_connection]
host_key_auto_add = True
```
